faqs.q: How much hair fall per day is normal?
faqs.a: Losing roughly 50 to 100 hairs a day is generally considered normal, because old hairs shed as new ones grow. It is worth seeing a dermatologist if you notice clumps coming out, patchy bald spots, a clearly widening parting or receding hairline, or shedding that continues for several weeks.

faqs.q: Will hair lost in my 20s grow back?
faqs.a: It depends on the cause. Shedding triggered by stress, illness, crash dieting or a nutrient deficiency usually grows back once the cause is dealt with. Hereditary pattern hair loss tends to be gradual and ongoing, but a dermatologist can suggest treatments that may slow it, and these generally work best when started early.

faqs.q: Do biotin or other supplements stop hair fall?
faqs.a: Supplements usually help only if you are actually low in a nutrient such as iron, vitamin D or certain B vitamins. Taking them without a deficiency is unlikely to make a difference, and some, like iron, can be harmful in excess, so ask a doctor to check your levels before starting any.

faqs.q: Does oiling hair reduce hair fall?
faqs.a: Oiling can soften the hair and reduce dryness and breakage, and a gentle scalp massage feels relaxing, but it does not treat hair loss from the roots caused by genetics, hormones, stress or deficiencies. If hair fall continues despite good hair care, see a dermatologist to find the underlying cause.
